reasons: Lake record identifies Garrity v. New Jersey as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1967 with official citation 385 U.S. 493.
The table holding is supported by the lake pinpoint stating that coerced statements obtained under threat of removal from office may not be used in subsequent criminal proceedings.
Lake record identifies Kalkines v. United States as a U.S. Court of Claims case decided in 1973 and includes 473 F.2d 1391 among its citations.
The holding matches the lake pinpoint requiring adequate notice both of discharge risk for non-answering and of criminal non-use of replies and fruits.
residual_risks: Lake official citation selection is null, but the cited F.2d citation, court, and year are present in the lake record.

reasons: Lake record identifies Gardner v. Broderick as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1968 with official citation 392 U.S. 273.

The lake pinpoint supports the duty-related-questions limitation and the no-waiver condition: questions must relate specifically, directly, and narrowly to official duties, without requiring waiver of immunity for answers or fruits.
residual_risks: Pinpoints are slip-only rather than star-verified, but the quoted lake passage supports the proposition.

reasons: Lake record identifies LaChance v. Erickson as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1998 with official citation 522 U.S. 262.

The table holding is supported by the lake pinpoints stating that an employee may remain silent if answering could expose him to criminal prosecution, but an agency may take adverse action for false statements in response to misconduct charges.
residual_risks: Lake status is under_review, but the identity and citation fields confirm the case citation.

reasons: Lake record identifies NASA v. FLRA as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1999 with official citation 527 U.S. 229.
Lake scope note and pinpoints support the statutory FSLMRS representation-right characterization and the NASA-OIG representative point.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the lake absolute_url for the opinion link while leaving the citation and holding intact.

reasons: Lake record identifies Lefkowitz v. Turley as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1973 with official citation 414 U.S. 70.
The lake scope note and pinpoint support the rule that the State must grant immunity rather than demand waiver and that answers elicited by threat of employment loss are compelled and inadmissible.
residual_risks: Pinpoints are slip-only rather than star-verified, but the quoted lake passage supports the proposition.

reasons: Lake record identifies Miranda v. Arizona as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 1966 with official citation 384 U.S. 436.

The lake pinpoint defines custodial interrogation as law-enforcement questioning after custody or equivalent deprivation of freedom, supporting the related-case placement as the custodial-interrogation counterpart.
residual_risks: The broader contrast to Garrity is supported by the Garrity-family lake records, not by a full Miranda text file.

reasons: Garrity pin-500 supports the core rule barring use in subsequent criminal proceedings of statements obtained under threat of removal from office.
Gardner pin-278 supports compelling official-duty answers without requiring waiver of immunity for answers or fruits.
Lefkowitz pin-84a supports both the no-waiver rule and the fruits point, stating that the State may not demand waiver and must offer immunity sufficient to supplant the privilege.
residual_risks: No text files were present; support was verified from lake pinpoints and judgment fields only.
